source_event.summary: The handoff lost independent-rejection history and omitted mandatory re-audit evidence.

generalized_learning.generalized_failure_pattern: A delivery reconstructs a readiness handoff after an independent rejection but classifies it as an initial handoff, bypassing the closure and cumulative-control requirements that only activate for re-audit.
generalized_learning.plausible_wrong_implementation: Regenerate a green certificate for the same functional candidate while leaving the previous-rejection state false and omitting audit escape, learning and inherited-control evidence.

reusable_control.description: A re-audit handoff must carry explicit prior-rejection state, closed audit escapes, learning closure and cumulative inherited controls before certificate publication.

generalized_learning.prevention_rule: Persist and propagate independent-rejection state into the delivery handoff path; do not allow certificate construction for a re-audit until audit escape closure, learning closure and cumulative inherited controls are complete.
generalized_learning.detection_rule: Fail readiness and terminal handoff validation when a re-audit lacks closure artifacts, inherited controls or a result-only certificate bound to the material candidate.

transfer_cases.scenario: A synthetic re-audit attempts certificate construction without the required learning or escape closure.
transfer_cases.evidence: Generic handoff certificate and audit escape contract tests passed and exercise fail-closed re-audit requirements.

transfer_cases.scenario: A synthetic published handoff child is stale, missing the certificate or not bound to the material parent.
transfer_cases.evidence: Generic terminal-handoff and connector-only contract tests passed and reject invalid published handoff identity.

skill_changes.evidence: The current generic delivery skill already requires learning closure for every independent rejection, cumulative inherited controls and certificate construction with previous-independent-rejection gates.
Generic readiness, handoff-certificate and terminal-handoff validators enforce missing-closure, missing-control and stale-publication failures; the focused contract suite passed 13 tests in this run.
